name: MonarchSplitButton
title: SplitButton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row of two MonarchButtons (androidx.compose.material3.Button) and MonarchMenu anchored to the arrow
summary: A main action joined to an arrow button that opens a menu of related alternatives, such as Save with Save as draft and Save and close.
whenToUse: When one action is the usual choice and a few close variants should stay one tap away without crowding the screen.
whenNotToUse: When there is no main action and the button only opens a menu, use the menu-button recipe (a MonarchButton with a MonarchMenu). For unrelated actions use separate buttons or a MonarchButtonGroup.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSplitButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, arrowIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, menuEnabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, moreOptionsLabel: String? = null, loadingLabel: String? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, menuContent: @Composable ColumnScope.(close: () -> Unit) -> Unit)

options.name: onClick
options.description: Runs the main action. Not called while loading or disabled.

options.name: arrowIcon
options.description: The arrow, for example a MonarchIcon of a chevron that points down with a null content description. Required because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: variant
options.description: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger, for both buttons.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm, Md or Lg, for both buttons. Each keeps a 48dp touch target.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Disables the main action and the menu together.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows progress on the main button and disables the arrow.

options.name: menuEnabled
options.description: Disables only the arrow, keeping the main action available.

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: An icon before the main label.

options.name: moreOptionsLabel
options.description: The TalkBack name of the arrow. Default: "More options for <text>" (monarch_splitbutton_more_options).

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: The state of the main button while loading. Default: the MonarchButton string "Loading".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interactions of the main button.

options.name: menuContent
options.description: The menu items, usually MonarchMenuItems; call close from an item to close the menu.

states.name: idle
states.description: Two buttons of the variant joined by a small gap; the menu is closed.

states.name: open
states.description: The MonarchMenu is shown under the arrow; the arrow's state is "Expanded".

states.name: loading
states.description: The main button shows progress and ignores taps; the arrow is disabled and an open menu closes.

states.name: menu disabled
states.description: The arrow uses the disabled colors; the main action still works.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both buttons use the disabled colors.

appearance: Both halves are MonarchButtons, so they take the colors of the variant: the accent fill for Primary, the surface with the default border for Secondary, no fill for Ghost, the danger fill for Danger, and the muted fill with the disabled text role when disabled. The menu is the Monarch menu on the raised background role. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web SplitButton draws the main button and a separate arrow button with its own Tab stop and the name "More options for <label>", with controlled open state and alignment. Android does the same with two MonarchButtons and a MonarchMenu; the open state is kept inside the component and closed with the close callback. The Material 3 SplitButtonLayout is experimental in Material 3 1.4, so Monarch does not use it and joins its own buttons with a small gap, which also keeps the Monarch variants and the loading state. The web items shorthand is replaced by MonarchMenuItems in menuContent. iOS uses the system Menu with a primary action, or a joined pair, as a style recipe.
accessibility: The main button and the arrow are separate TalkBack elements with the Button role; the pair is a traversal group.
The arrow is named "More options for Save" by default and reports "Expanded" or "Collapsed" as its state, with the expand and collapse accessibility actions.
While loading, the main button keeps its place in the focus order and reports "Loading".
Each button keeps a 48dp touch target at every size; the arrow icon slot should be decorative (null content description).
edgeCases: A long label wraps inside the main button; the arrow keeps its size.
The menu closes when the arrow becomes disabled and stays closed when it comes back.
Items must call close themselves; the menu also closes on back and on a tap outside.

examples.title: Primary with alternatives
Main action available, menu disabled
examples.code:
MonarchSplitButton(
    text = "Export",
    onClick = {},
    arrowIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ChevronDown, contentDescription = null) },
    menuEnabled = false,
) { close ->
    MonarchMenuItem(text = "Export as PDF", onClick = close)
}
